newsitem.title: USA: Winn-Dixie boosts size of average store.
newsitem.headline: Winn-Dixie boosts size of average store.

text.p: Winn-Dixie Stores Inc said on Wednesday it has boosted the average size of its stores to 40,000 square feet, which it described as a milestone.

"We have been able to add many services to our one-stop shopping concept," company President James Kufeldt said in a statement. "Our store managers have committed the necessary resources to build sales. This has affected our operation short-term, but we are excited abut the long-term potential."
Winn-Dixie said it opened 61 new stores averaging 50,000 square feet during the first 40 weeks of fiscal 1997, enlarged or remodeled 63 stores and closed 58 stores averaging 29,000 square feet.
The company said it plans to open 24 new stores and enlarge or remodel 27 during the fourth quarter.
Winn-Dixie reported third quarter net income of $0.38 per share, down from $0.42 a year ago but above the First Call estimate of $0.36.
